claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix microstructure.
Degradation is governed by a gas-composition-induced transition between protective oxide-scale formation and detrimental internal phase transformation.
A stable oxide layer forms in oxidizing environments.
The oxide layer formed in oxidizing environments protects the alloy against further degradation.
More reducing conditions compromise the protective oxide layer.
Compromising the oxide layer promotes grain-boundary phase changes.
Grain-boundary phase changes produce brittle failure and can culminate in catastrophic failure.
The reactive gas composition will be varied by changing oxygen partial pressure relative to hydrogen or inert diluents.
Exposure will cover 700–1000°C and atmospheres ranging from oxidizing to moderately reducing.
Changing gas composition alters the oxidation–reduction balance at the alloy surface.
A protective oxide scale under highly oxidizing conditions mitigates internal phase changes.
Reduced oxygen availability triggers grain-boundary phase transformations through formation of a less protective oxide scale.
Predominantly oxidizing exposure will produce a robust, uniform oxide layer and minimal internal phase transformation.
More reducing exposure will produce less protective oxide scales and increased grain-boundary brittle-phase formation.
Samples exposed to more reducing atmospheres will undergo earlier mechanical failure than the as-built baseline.
The proposed exposure durations are sufficient to activate diffusion-controlled oxidation and phase-transformation kinetics.
